transcript:
Meeting: StrataForge discovery — quickstart, hosting constraints, and pilot path
Date/Time: 2026-07-31 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sarah Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (StrataForge CTO), Marcus Novak (StrataForge ML Eng), Priya Singh (StrataForge Head of Platform)
Recording link: https://redwood.example/rec/ff-20260731-8421 (internal)

Summary:
- Customer evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for low-latency inference in production; high interest in quickstart/free credits and time-to-first-token (TTFT).
- Key constraints: VPC peering/egress controls, KMS integration for secrets, SOC 2 & audit expectations, and predictable tail latency under burst.
- Agreed next steps: send pricing + pilot contract, benchmark sheet, quickstart runbook; pilot kickoff targeted week of 2026-08-10.

Topics Covered:
- Quickstart flow, free credits, TTFT expectations
- Hosting modes: hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Security: KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data retention
- Performance: batching, KV cache, tail latency, burst behavior
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Kim (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros from our side, I'm Sarah, AE at Redwood, and Diego's our SE who will talk performance and pilot details.
[00:18] Laura Chen (StrataForge): Hi all, Laura here. We're trying to get a clear path to production, so appreciate the time.
[00:23] Marcus Novak (StrataForge): Marcus, ML eng — I'll own evaluation and perf.
[00:27] Priya Singh (StrataForge): Priya, platform. We'll be focused on networking and security.
[00:33] Diego Ramos (Redwood): Great. Quick agenda: quickstart/credits for TTFT, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, security checklist, and propose a pilot scope.
[00:45] Laura: Sounds good. We're piloting a customer-facing summarization feature — latency matters, also PII in some docs so data residency and encryption are blockers.
[00:58] Sarah: Understood. For TTFT, most customers can get to first token in under an hour via our PLG quickstart when they use free credits and self-serve API — assuming no private network setup.
[01:12] Marcus: That's the thing — our infra will probably require VPC peering and strict egress rules. How much friction is that?
[01:21] Diego: If you need VPC, that's usually Redwood Private — we do a private control plane and customer-managed network. That requires an ops window to set up and often adds a few days for access and firewall changes. Hosted is immediate and simplest for TTFT.
[01:36] Priya: For compliance we need KMS integration and audit logs. Do hosted customers get KMS?
[01:44] Sarah: Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit; we offer customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated via KMS integrations. For hosted we have envelope encryption but not customer-managed keys by default — could explore dedicated offering if CMK is required.
[01:59] Laura: Hmm okay. We're trying to decide if we should start on hosted for speed, then move to dedicated once committed. Any pitfalls?
[02:08] Diego: That's common — start hosted with pseudonymous data or scrubbed inputs, use free credits to validate model quality and throughput. Then for production you can migrate to Dedicated to get reserved GPU pools and KMS, plus better tail latency SLAs. We do have migration patterns documented.
[02:24] Marcus: Can you quantify tail latency improvements with Dedicated vs hosted? We need p95 under 350ms for 1k qps bursts in our SLA model.
[02:34] Diego: p95 is a tough one to promise without workload specifics. In general, Dedicated with pinned capacity and optimized batching reduces variability. We usually see median token times similar across modes, but tail variability is better with reserved capacity. We'll share benchmark sheets — need your request mix and sequence lengths.
[02:52] Priya: About network — we have strict firewall egress rules. Does Redwood require outbound 443 only, or are there extra ports for streaming or KV cache?
[03:03] Sarah: For hosted, outbound 443 to our endpoints. For Private, you'll peer and it's within your VPC, so rules differ. Some internal ops require additional ports for metrics/observability if you want agent-based telemetry, but core inference is over TLS.
[03:18] Laura: SOC 2 — our security team asked for SOC 2 Type II and an understanding of your incident response. Do you have those docs?
[03:26] Sarah: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs; Diego can drop the security pack. Also we offer SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs as part of enterprise packages.
[03:37] Diego: I'll share our security pack and the SOC 2 report redacted. Also the compliance page that lists encryption defaults and data retention.
[03:45] Marcus: On perf testing — what does your batching and KV cache strategy look like? Does it break deterministic latency?
[03:54] Diego: We do continuous batching with a latency-aware scheduler. There's also prefix KV caching for conversational contexts. For low-latency single-turn queries, you can tune batching windows or pin to Dedicated capacity. There is a tradeoff: more batching lowers cost but can increase median latency slightly.
[04:13] Laura: For the pilot we want to validate both quality and latency for the summarization workload. What's a typical pilot scope?
[04:20] Sarah: Typical pilot: 2–4 week sprint, we provide free credits for hosted evaluation, share quickstart guide, you run a synthetic and real traffic run, Redwood SE helps with basic tuning, and we run a benchmark that you can compare to your SLA. If you need KMS or VPC we'll propose a Dedicated trial (30-day) or Private evaluation depending on timelines.
[04:40] Priya: Licensing and pricing — is there an upfront for Dedicated? What's the commitment?
[04:46] Sarah: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits; pricing varies by GPU type and capacity. For pilots we sometimes do a short-term reserved pool or provide discounted eval credits for Dedicated. We'll surface precise numbers in the pricing doc.
[04:59] Marcus: Any competitors or migration lock-in we should be worried about? We use Vertex internally for some ML glue.
[05:06] Diego: No model lock-in: we support multiple models and can export logs and traces. Competitors mentioned here are Anthropic/OpenAI/Vertex for managed endpoints; Redwood differentiates on production controls and cost tuning.
[05:20] Laura: About TTFT, you said under an hour typically — can you walk through steps for us to hit first token quickly?
[05:27] Sarah: Sure: 1) Sign up with your company email and claim free credits; 2) Create API key in console; 3) Use quickstart curl or SDK snippet — a standard request to the hosted endpoint should return first token in <60 minutes including account setup. If you need SSO or company billing it'll add time.
[05:45] Marcus: SDKs — do you have Java and Python? We'll want Python and Node.
[05:49] Diego: Yes, official SDKs for Python, Node; community ones for Java. We'll link to sample repos.
[05:54] Priya: What's the observability story? We need request-level tracing and cost per token.
[05:59] Diego: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency dashboards, traces, and request logs with retention configurable in enterprise tiers.
[06:10] Laura: For the pilot, we need to run a burst test to see tail behavior. Can Redwood run the benchmark or do we run and send data?
[06:18] Sarah: We can run benchmarks jointly. Diego can provide a benchmark sheet and a runner script; your team provides realistic traffic and we'll help interpret results.
[06:26] Marcus: About data residency — some of our customers are EU-only. Can we get EU hosting?
[06:30] Sarah: Yes, we have regional endpoints in EU and NA; for strict data residency Private may be recommended. We'll note that in the pilot plan.
[06:39] Priya: Small thing — log retention policy and ability to disable logging for PII payloads?
[06:44] Diego: You can opt out of request logging for hosted in enterprise contracts, and Private puts you in control. We'll include the logging controls in the security pack.
[06:54] Laura: Great. Let's talk timing: we want to get an experiment in prod beta in 6 weeks. Is that realistic?
[07:01] Sarah: For a hosted-based pilot, yes — 2–4 weeks to validate, additional time to integrate. If you need Dedicated/Private, add setup time for network and KMS integration (typically 2–3 weeks).
[07:12] Marcus: Regarding model selection — are you recommending specific open models or Redwood-curated ones?
[07:17] Diego: We have a model catalog with curated open models optimized for inference and Redwood-verified performance profiles. For summarization we'll recommend a smaller transformer with quantization profile to reduce latency. We'll attach model recommendations in the benchmark sheet.
[07:32] Laura: Costs — can you ballpark per-1k-requests for hosted vs dedicated? Even approximate ranges help us budget.
[07:40] Sarah: We'll give ranges in pricing doc — hosted per-token usage, Dedicated has committed hourly capacity and lower per-token marginal cost. For pilots we provide credits to get initial numbers.
[07:51] Priya: Do you have an SLA for hosted? Or only Dedicated?
[07:56] Diego: SLA is part of Dedicated/enterprise packages. Hosted has best-effort SLAs; for strict uptime/latency SLAs use Dedicated.
[08:05] Laura: Security review — our legal asked about subprocessors and data flow diagrams.
[08:11] Sarah: We'll include subprocessors and an architecture diagram in the security pack.
[08:17] Marcus: One technical question: how do you handle KV cache eviction with long-running conversations? We do long context summaries sometimes.
[08:26] Diego: We maintain per-request KV with LRU eviction and configurable cache TTL; for very long contexts we recommend explicit KV checkpointing and chunking. There's a tradeoff with memory on Dedicated.
[08:41] Priya: Do you support bringing your own HSM?
[08:44] Diego: For Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSM/KMS; Dedicated can use cloud KMS solutions. Hosted cannot directly plug into a customer HSM.
[08:55] Laura: Ok. I think the sequence for us will be: 1) sign up hosted evaluation with scrubbed data, 2) run Redwood-provided benchmark, 3) if performance and security align, spin a Dedicated pilot.
[09:08] Sarah: That sounds like a good plan. We'll send a pilot plan and the necessary docs.
[09:12] Marcus: If possible, include a baseline comparison to Vertex endpoints in the sheet.
[09:17] Diego: We can add a column for Vertex/OpenAI comparisons based on public perf numbers; for strict apples-to-apples we'd need your traffic.
[09:27] Priya: Can we get a short checklist of firewall rules and SSO steps?
[09:32] Sarah: Yes — Diego will include a network checklist and SSO steps in the runbook.
[09:38] Laura: Any blockers from your side to getting us TTFT quickly?
[09:41] Sarah: Not really for hosted. For SSO or company billing you'll need admin approvals; for Private we'll need an ops contact for peering.
[09:50] Marcus: Two small asks — sample curl + SDK snippets with chunked streaming, and a recommended quantization profile for the model you suggest.
[09:58] Diego: We'll include both in the runbook. The quantization recs vary by GPU type but we'll give recommended configs.
[10:06] Laura: Great. That answers most of our questions. Anything else from Redwood?
[10:10] Sarah: We'll produce three documents after this call: 1) Pricing + pilot contract draft; 2) Security pack (SOC2, subprocessors, architecture, logging controls); 3) Benchmark sheet + quickstart runbook with SDK snippets. Expect those within 3–5 business days.
[10:26] Priya: Good. We'll align internally and aim to confirm pilot participants and firewall owners by early next week.
[10:33] Laura: Let's tentatively target a kickoff the week of Aug 10th.
[10:37] Sarah: Works for us. Diego, anything to add?
[10:40] Diego: I'll add a short checklist for the performance test and include a pre-built runner script. I'll also share a small sample dataset format so it's straightforward to run.
[10:49] Marcus: Appreciate it. One note — we may request a short Dedicated eval if we see variance in hosted during benchmark.
[10:55] Sarah: Noted. We'll prepare options for a short Dedicated trial and what that entails contractually.
[11:02] Laura: Thanks everyone.
[11:04] Sarah: Thanks — we will follow up with the docs and proposed dates.

Recap (end of call):
- Redwood to send: pricing + pilot contract draft, security pack (SOC2, logging controls, subprocessors), benchmark sheet + quickstart runbook + SDK snippets, network checklist.
- Customer to: confirm firewall owners and pilot participants, build sample prompt set and anonymized test data, decide whether to start hosted or request a Dedicated eval after hosted benchmark.
- Target pilot kickoff: week of 2026-08-10.

Action items (as logged):
- Sarah Kim: Send pricing + pilot contract draft by 2026-08-03.
- Diego Ramos: Share benchmark spreadsheet, quickstart runbook, SDK examples, and network checklist by 2026-08-04.
- Priya Singh: Confirm firewall rules and ops contact by 2026-08-05.

End of transcript.
